style: Say calmly and clearly, like a kind crossing guard teaching young children safety
lines: Biscuit wants to cross the street to the park. What should Biscuit do?
One: Hold a grown-up's hand, stop at the curb and look left, right, left.
Two: Hold a grown-up's hand, stop at the curb and look left, right, left.
One: Run across fast before a car comes.
Two: Run across fast before a car comes.
Stop at the curb. Look left, right and left again. Cross with a grown-up at the crosswalk.
Running into the street is dangerous. Drivers might not see you. Always stop at the curb first.
Biscuit is going for a bike ride. What comes first?
One: Put on a helmet and buckle the strap.
Two: Put on a helmet and buckle the strap.
One: Ride without a helmet just this once.
Two: Ride without a helmet just this once.
A helmet protects your brain. Wear it every time you ride a bike, scooter or skateboard.
Even a short ride can have a fall. Helmets go on every time.
Biscuit gets in the car to go to Grandma's house.
One: Sit in the car seat or booster and buckle up.
Two: Sit in the car seat or booster and buckle up.
One: Stand up and look out the window.
Two: Stand up and look out the window.
Buckle up every ride, in the back seat, in your car seat or booster.
If the car stops fast, an unbuckled rider can get hurt. Click it every time!
BEEP BEEP BEEP! The fire alarm is ringing at school!
One: Leave your things, line up and walk outside with your teacher.
Two: Leave your things, line up and walk outside with your teacher.
One: Hide under the table until it stops.
Two: Hide under the table until it stops.
Get out fast and stay out. Go to your meeting place and listen to your teacher.
Never hide in a fire. Firefighters need to find you outside. Get out and stay out.
A pot is cooking on the stove. Biscuit wants to see what's inside.
One: Stay back and ask a grown-up.
Two: Stay back and ask a grown-up.
One: Reach up and grab the pot handle.
Two: Reach up and grab the pot handle.
Stoves and pots can be very hot. Stay three big steps back and ask a grown-up.
A hot pot can burn you or spill. Kids stay back from the stove.
It's a hot day at the pool! Biscuit wants to jump in.
One: Wait until a grown-up is watching, and wear a life jacket.
Two: Wait until a grown-up is watching, and wear a life jacket.
One: Jump in the deep end alone.
Two: Jump in the deep end alone.
Swim only when a grown-up is watching. A life jacket helps you float.
Never swim alone. A grown-up must always be watching the water.
Biscuit finds a bottle of colorful pills. They look like candy!
One: Don't touch it, and tell a grown-up.
Two: Don't touch it, and tell a grown-up.
One: Try one to see if it tastes good.
Two: Try one to see if it tastes good.
Medicine is not candy. Only take medicine from a grown-up you trust.
Medicine can make you very sick if it isn't meant for you. Tell a grown-up instead.
Safe choice!
Not safe.
Biscuit made it all the way down Safety Street. You helped make safe choices at every stop!
Wear a helmet on your scooter.
Play with matches or a lighter.
Buckle your seat belt.
Swim when no grown-up is watching.
Hold a grown-up's hand in a parking lot.
Take medicine because it looks like candy.
Stop at the curb and look both ways.
Chase a ball into the street.
Get out and stay out when the fire alarm rings.
Touch a hot stove.
Wear a life jacket on a boat.
Ride your bike without a helmet.
Tell a grown-up if you find something sharp.
Hide during a fire drill.
Know your grown-up's phone number.
Stand up in a moving car.
Safe, or not safe?
Yes!
Think again.
That is safe.
That is not safe.
Stop at the curb. Wait for the walking person.
Look left first, then right, then left again.
Left.
Right.
Left again.
Keep looking while you cross!
Safe on the other side!
The walking person is on!
